text:
riley: Heads-up — the weekly dashboard shows a weird post-webinar bump in demo signups (roughly +40%) but CRM shows only a small change. Can we sanity-check attribution window + UTM handling? :thinking_face:

aisha: Noted. Which dashboard panel? I can pull the raw hits and convs. :bar_chart:

riley: Panel link: https://dash.redwood.com/d/metrics/webinar-ops?panelId=7 — the conversion rate line jumps right after the webinar ended at 15:05 UTC.

tom: I ran a quick grep on server logs and saw a batch of requests with missing utm_source that fell back to "ref=internal_newsletter" around the same time. Might be our landing page rewrite that changed the query param names.

nina: I also checked the ETL - we collapse leads by email in the enrichment step and attribute to first-touch if utm_source exists, else use referrer. If referrer changed to internal_newsletter it would count as webinar-sourced in the dashboard.

riley: OK that would explain the spike in the dashboard but not in CRM (CRM uses lead-created timestamp + manual source). We need to decide whether weekly KPI should stick to first-touch or switch to last-touch for demo signups.

aisha: For this week I'd prefer we mark those as "unattributed-webinar-tmp" until we fix the landing page and ETL. That prevents noisy KPI shifts during the next exec review.

tom: +1. I can patch the ETL to map internal_newsletter -> null for the temporary rollup. Patch SQL below I tested locally: 

```sql
-- treat legacy query param fallback as unknown source during rollup
UPDATE staging.leads SET utm_source = NULL
WHERE utm_source = 'internal_newsletter' AND created_at >= '2026-03-10';
```

nina: Thanks. I'll push a transformation rule in Airflow to enforce that for weekly aggregates and add a note to the dashboard description. Also adding a regression check so future landing page refactors fail the QA gate.

dashbot: deploy-bot: ETL patch queued for airflow/transformations/2026-03-10-utm-fix (run window: next 01:00 UTC).

riley: Can someone add a one-line blurb to the weekly KPI email explaining the temporary correction? Execs noticed the spike in the draft.

aisha: I'll update the email: "We identified a UTM-referrer fallback that inflated dashboard demo signups post-webinar. We've adjusted weekly aggregates and are rolling a permanent fix. No material change to CRM counts."

tom: Quick follow-ups: (1) revert landing page param rename or add mapping, (2) add a dashboard annotation for the event, (3) schedule a 20-min postmortem in this channel tomorrow.

nina: I'll create the dashboard annotation and add a Prometheus alert to detect >25% delta between dashboard and CRM weekly counts.

riley: Thank you all — appreciate the fast triage. Let's keep the postmortem focused on process: how did the param rename get missed and how to avoid noisy KPI regressions. :white_check_mark:
